sentences.text: Khaan is an extinct oviraptorid dinosaur that lived during the Late Cretaceous period in Mongolia.
This animal looked very similar to other members of its family.
Evidence suggests the creature was covered in feathers.
The primary specimens discovered together measured only about four feet in length.
However, a third individual found at the site was significantly larger than the main group.
For a time, this genus held the record for the shortest non-avian dinosaur name before newer discoveries changed the ranking.
Scientists formally named the species Khaan mckennai in the year 2001.
The specific name mckennai was chosen to honor the paleontologist Malcolm Carnegie McKenna.
Fossils were unearthed in the Djadokhta Formation of Mongolia, where the holotype consists of an almost complete skeleton that was slightly separated in the chest area.
Recent research from 2022 indicates that Khaan had a bite force much stronger than other oviraptorosaurs.
Although a moderate jaw opening often points to a plant-based diet, this animal likely ate tougher vegetation than other herbivorous theropods.
It is also probable that the dinosaur ate small vertebrates such as mammals, lizards, and perhaps other tiny dinosaurs.
A study published in Nature in 2014 proposed that the species might show sexual dimorphism.
Scientists believed that smaller chevron spines might belong to females because they would allow more room for laying eggs.
Conversely, larger chevron spines were thought to support muscle attachments for males, potentially aiding a tail fan.
This dinosaur belongs to the family Oviraptoridae.
Within the oviraptorid group, Khaan appears to be more closely related to Conchoraptor.
It can be distinguished from Conchoraptor by several features in the nasal region.
A reduction in the third metacarpal bone is a unique trait of Khaan mckennai, unless the lower limb bones are not specialized.
Unlike Ajancingenia, the first metacarpal of Khaan is not extremely wide.
Khaan lived approximately 72 million years ago during the Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous in what is now Asia.
The estimated time range for this species spans from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago.
The exact diet of oviraptorids like Khaan remains a topic of discussion, with suggestions ranging from plants to molluscs.
Examinations suggest these dinosaurs may have been either powerful-biting generalists or specialists utilizing niche partitioning based on body size and cranial function.
